speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what is happening, have you noticed any specific triggers for this pain, such as touching the earlobe or lying on that side?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent infections and the timing of your pain, did you experience any fluid drainage, itching, or a sensation of fullness in the right ear immediately following your tympanoplasty surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent mastoiditis with potential graft failure or tympanic membrane perforation secondary to chronic otitis media.
